recentItems.title: How cooking together preserves more than family recipes | Staci Perry Mergenthal | TEDxSioux Falls
recentItems.description:
What if the most important part of a family recipe isn’t written down? Midwest food storyteller Staci Perry Mergenthal discovered this while learning her grandma’s cherished white cookie recipe side-by-side in her kitchen. The experience revealed that the true heart of a recipe lives in the things we learn together—the techniques, textures, stories, and shared experience. In this talk, Staci shows how baking alongside someone we love passes down more than recipes; it preserves stories, tradition, and belonging. 

Staci Perry Mergenthal is a Midwest storyteller, writer, and home baker who explores how everyday recipes carry stories and connections across generations. She is the producer and host of the podcast Funeral Potatoes & Wool Mittens and creator of the blog Random Sweets, where she shares recipes, food stories, and the warm spirit of Midwest living. A frequent guest on KELOLAND Living and a contributor to Food Network, Taste of Home, and regional magazines, Staci speaks about how baking together passes down more than recipes—it preserves stories, tradition, and belonging. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: History has no memory of echoes | Christopher Yaw Annor Adu-Gyimah | TEDxAshesi University
recentItems.description: In Plato's allegory of the cave, the prisoner who escapes is mocked by those still inside. This talk applies that to how success is defined in this part of the world: an "office syndrome" that prizes how a career looks and pays over the change it creates, and a "trifecta career trap" of doctor, lawyer, or engineer. It offers three reminders for anyone going their own way: they will laugh, ask questions because there is no instruction manual, and post, because visibility now matters more than quality Christopher Yaw Annor Adu-Gyimah is the founder and CEO of Manna by Nabiy, a premium gourmet cookie and baked goods brand he built from a campus operation into a growing commercial venture. A History graduate of the University of Ghana, he is currently a student at Ashesi University, Class of 2030. Known online as Nabiy the Cookie Billionaire, he has built a following of tens of thousands across TikTok and Instagram, with several videos crossing one million views. Alongside Manna by Nabiy, he has researched and developed green energy applications, including converting biomass and coconut husks into eco-friendly briquettes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to Be a Copy Cat | Nubuke Gadzekpo Amoah | TEDxAshesi University
recentItems.description: Every original idea started as a copy of something else. This talk argues that copying, done well, is how creativity works: steal the architecture of an idea instead of its surface, observe closely before you act, and recreate it knowing that every copy comes out different, the way one cassava root becomes gari, attiéké, tapioca, and farofa across cultures Nubuke Gadzekpo Amoah is a content creator and creative strategist with years of experience in digital storytelling. He has been creating content since 2018, building a community of more than 70,000 followers across YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram. He has held digital communications roles at the Ghana Center for Democratic Development and the Media Foundation for West Africa, and currently serves as Senior Analyst, Digital Content and Engagement Lead at IC Group. His work reflects years of quietly building something real in a fast-moving attention economy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: This little kitchen in Sicily could feed the world | Danny McCubbin | TEDxBoston
recentItems.description: Hunger is a hidden crisis, compounded by shame and isolation. Over 280,000 people in Sicily access a food bank every month, and many more in need likely do not reach for available assistance. Meanwhile, we waste a third of the food we produce. One concept is looking to solve this intersecting challenge: a community kitchen in a rural Italian village proves that rescued food, cooked with care, can have amplifing effect by fighting hunger, reducing waste, and rebuilding community at the same time. After five years in operation, this kitchen had rescued 29 tons of food, served 10,000 meals, and turned a crumbling town square into a table where everyone is welcome. Now imagine that model in every town on Earth. You don't have to be a chef to lend a hand. This is stone soup in action, where technology can take this grassroots blueprint and make it a turn-key solution on a global scale, where everyone has a seat at the table. Danny McCubbin, an award-winning author, food campaigner, and overall passionate advocate for social change, is the visionary behind The Good Kitchen in Italy, redefining the meaning of community and sustainability in the culinary world. With years of experience working alongside renowned chefs, including Jamie Oliver, Danny has dedicated his career to combining his love for food with a mission to make a difference. The Good Kitchen is more than a place to enjoy delicious meals; it’s a community-focused initiative that uses food as a tool for connection and healing. Based in Mussomeli, Italy, a country celebrated for its culinary heritage, Danny has created a space where sustainability meets compassion, offering free meals to those in need and championing zero-waste practices. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Биеэ засаад гэрээ зас | Altankhuyag Norov | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description:
Meaningful change begins with the individual. Drawing upon the traditional Mongolian philosophy of self-cultivation, Norovyn Altankhuyag invites us to reconsider the relationship between personal development, family responsibility, and social progress.

In a world where people often seek to transform their surroundings, this talk encourages us to first examine our own values, decisions, habits, and responsibilities. It explores the idea that building a stronger family and a better society begins with developing personal integrity, self-discipline, and a deeper awareness of our actions.

By connecting traditional wisdom with the challenges of contemporary life, the talk offers a perspective on how individual growth can contribute to collective well-being. Ultimately, it invites us to recognize that meaningful and sustainable change is not merely something we expect from others, but something that begins within ourselves. Altankhuyag Norov is a Mongolian politician, former Prime Minister of Mongolia (2012–2014), and Member of the State Great Khural. He graduated from the National University of Mongolia with a specialization in biophysics in 1981 and subsequently worked as a university lecturer until 1990. Throughout his career in public service, he has held several senior government positions, including Minister of Agriculture and Industry, Minister of Finance, and First Deputy Prime Minister. His professional background spans scientific education, public administration, governance, and national policymaking. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: A Dispatch from the Universe | Anarsaikhan Ariunbat | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description:
What can the vastness of the universe reveal about humanity and our place within it? In this talk, Anarsaikhan Ariunbat invites us to look beyond the familiar boundaries of everyday life and consider the profound questions that emerge from our exploration of the cosmos.

Through the lens of astronomy, the talk encourages us to reflect on the relationship between scientific discovery, human curiosity, and our understanding of existence. As humanity continues to investigate the mysteries of the universe, each discovery offers not only new scientific knowledge but also an opportunity to reconsider our perspective on the world.

By connecting cosmic exploration with the human pursuit of understanding, this talk highlights the importance of curiosity and scientific inquiry. It invites us to appreciate the extraordinary complexity of the universe and recognize how much remains to be discovered beyond the limits of our current knowledge. A Mongolian high school student passionate about space science, aerospace engineering, science, and technology — learning by building with his own hands through rocketry, electronics, and 3D-printing projects, with the goal of contributing to the growth of Mongolia’s space technology sector. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What Is Self-Interest? | Dalai Davaadorj | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description: What do we mean when we say someone is acting in their own interest? Dalai Davaadorj invites the audience to examine the motives behind that familiar phrase. Hi, my name is Dalai. I am a student at Ulaanbaatar Empathy School, a content creator, and an aspiring psychology student. I enjoy documenting my life and socializing with others. I always look for new challenges that push me outside my comfort zone. I hope to be acquaintances or friends with every person on earth. recentItems.title: An Algorithm Beyond Time | Oyunbaatar Baatarkhuu | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description:
A network drawn with dots and lines can look surprisingly like the veins of a leaf. Baatarkhuu Oyunbaatar uses graph theory to explore what these patterns have in common and how mathematics can describe the connections we see in nature. I'm a competitive mathematician and graph theory practitioner from Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, specializing in discrete mathematics and network structures. My work explores how vertices and edges map complex systems, turning abstract mathematical concepts into intuitive frameworks and practical solutions.
I'm passionate about making high-level mathematics accessible, intuitive, and real-world relevant. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Nature Doesn’t Have Subjects | Byambadorj Mendbayar | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description:
Why do we divide knowledge into separate subjects when the natural world itself recognizes no such boundaries? Byambadorj Mendbayar challenges the conventional separation of academic disciplines and invites us to reconsider how we understand the interconnected nature of knowledge.

This talk explores the idea that mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology are not isolated fields, but complementary ways of understanding the same complex world. While traditional education often organizes knowledge into distinct categories, real-world phenomena rarely fit within a single discipline. By encouraging interdisciplinary thinking, the talk highlights the importance of looking beyond conventional academic boundaries and recognizing meaningful connections between different areas of learning.

Ultimately, it invites us to reconsider the purpose of education: not simply to accumulate knowledge within individual subjects, but to develop a more integrated, curious, and comprehensive understanding of the world around us. I have won two silver medals at the international Chemistry Olympiad, qualified for the international Biology Olympiad, and earned gold in Mongolian National Biology and silver in National Physics. I won MNB's Scientific Quiz Show '100%.' and scored 800, 800, 800, and 795 in Mongolia's national entrance examination in Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, and Biology This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: Beyond the Thin Line | Gabriel Balane | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description:
What separates us can also become an opportunity to connect. In this talk, Gabriel Balane explores the significance of embracing different perspectives, looking beyond cultural boundaries, and discovering common ground through mutual understanding. He encourages us to approach differences with curiosity and openness rather than assumptions. Mabuhay! My name is Gabriel and I am from the Philippines.
I currently study at GCF International Christian School and it is an honor be part of this event where we can create an environment where we get to share our ideas together freely.
Truly, it is so beautiful when people from different backgrounds come together. I hope to learn a lot about Mongolia during our stay here and to enable a melting pot of cultural fusion. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Bridging the Three Worlds | Davaa Shijir | TEDxUlaanbaatar Empathy School Youth
recentItems.description: The land around Shijir Davaa’s grandmother’s home in Dundgovi was changing. A satellite image could show that change, but what would it take for people to act on it? Shijir explores how scientists, local communities and environmental organizations can bring different kinds of knowledge to the same decision. I grew up watching the landscape around my grandmother's land in Dundgovi province change, long before I understood why. Today I study land degradation through satellite imagery data and work with scientists, communities, and environmental organizations. Along the way, I've found myself moving between worlds that don't always speak to each other This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Color Without Commentary | Zeta Raniry Abidin | TEDxITS
recentItems.description: We live in a world that asks us to explain before we begin. To frame our intentions before we act. To justify our choices before anyone has seen what they become. But what happens when the most meaningful things we make, and the most meaningful choices we take are the ones that cannot be fully explained before they arrive? Color Without Commentary is an exploration of what it means to act from a place of genuine presence. Not performing sincerity, but actually arriving in a room, in a decision, in a life without waiting for the perfect explanation to lead the way. Because the brushstroke that changes everything does not pause to justify itself. It simply moves. And in moving, it becomes true. This talk asks one question: what have you been holding back waiting until you were certain it could be explained? Zeta Ranniry Abidin is a young Indonesian painter from Surabaya whose work has always moved before she fully understood where it was going. A graduate of Universitas Kristen Maranatha, she has held four solo exhibitions, received the Bronze Award at the UOB Painting of the Year Competition 2023, and shown her work at ARTJOG, Art Jakarta, and ARTSUBS — not by waiting for the right moment, but by choosing, again and again, to let the canvas speak before the explanation was ready. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
